correctness.rationale: Every petal has a nonzero localized antisymmetric cycle eigenvector, establishing an unavoidable separate vertex input in each petal by PBH. For the proposed k-input set, zero readout forces the common recurrence f_j=-U_{j-2}((2-lambda)/2) with f_m=1 and hence |2-lambda|<2. Trigonometric factorization gives opposite-neighbor readout either 0 or (2-lambda)h. The hub identity 2(k-1)=(s-1)(2-lambda) is inconsistent for every integer 0<=s<=k, ruling out every unobservable eigenvector. Zero forcing lower/upper bounds follow from first-activation and explicit chain forcing. The independent finite checker passed 4595 exact modular Kalman rank and forcing assertions; it is not used as proof of all parameters.

originality.rationale: The finding is a uniform optimal-input classification for every arbitrary-length single-hub cycle bouquet, with a PBH coupling obstruction at the hub and a strict gap from ordinary zero forcing. Inspected Parlangeli--Notarstefano papers treat individual cycles/paths and Cartesian grids. Dai et al. provide general critical-eigenvector machinery but no direct mixed-length bouquet formula in inspected sections. An earlier published finding contains an all-triangle friendship zero-forcing formula, so that special case is explicitly treated as covered and not the claimed novelty. Three plausible papers lack accessible full text; an equivalent specialization remains a material risk, but no identified theorem implies the general mixed-length statement.
residual_risks: Full text of Liu--Ji 2017 could contain the specific bouquet family under another name; its abstract mentions other path/cycle-derived topologies.
Full text of Dong et al. 2023 and Guo et al. 2024 could establish all-triangle or other windmill special cases; none was declared absent.
Unindexed control-theory or graph-spectral literature could contain a stronger general bouquet classification.
The all-triangle Z(F_k)=k+1 special case is covered in a previously published zero-forcing-polynomial result and is excluded from the novelty assertion.

value.rationale: Exact optimal vertex actuation on single-articulation multi-cycle networks is natural and not merely a numerical example. A uniform answer k holds over all unequal petal sizes, with explicit placement and a strict k versus k+1 separation from the standard sufficient zero-forcing certificate. This matters in networks where each independently controlled vertex has a separate actuator cost. The nonstandard coupled-eigenmode hub contradiction is required for the upper bound; neither a generic PBH test nor the localized-eigenvector lower bound alone gives it. No energy or strong-structural robustness result is claimed.
